names.display_en: Kublai Khan, Emperor Shizu of Yuan

summary: 灭宋完成大一统，建国号大元、定都大都，以行省与站赤制度塑造后世格局的征服王朝皇帝。
summary_en: A conquest-dynasty emperor who destroyed the Song to complete a grand unification, proclaimed the dynastic name Great Yuan, fixed the capital at Dadu, and shaped later ages through the provincial and postal-relay systems.

bio_md:
# 元世祖 · 主要事迹

忽必烈是把蒙古汗国改写为中原式王朝、并完成唐亡以来再度大一统的皇帝。本页以《元史·世祖本纪》（卷004–017）为年表主线，平宋一段辅以《宋史·瀛国公纪》《二王本纪》对照。

他的开局是一场汗位内战：中统元年（1260）即大汗位于开平，建元中统，随即与阿里不哥争位并胜出。此后汉地制度逐步推进：至元元年（1264）改元，至元八年（1271）取《易》「大哉乾元」之义建国号大元，至元九年（1272）改中都为大都，政治中心落定燕地。

灭宋是其在位中段的主线：至元十年（1273）襄阳破，打开南下关键节点；至元十三年（1276）伯颜入临安，宋廷降，残部入海；至元十六年（1279）崖山之战，宋亡，中国再度大一统于元。与[[qin-shi-huang|秦始皇]]对读，可见两次大一统之间的长线呼应；与[[n-song-tai-zu|宋太祖]]对读，则见赵宋开国与终结的首尾。

他的武功也有边界：至元十八年（1281）再征日本，东征舰队遇风灾而败，扩张受挫。真正影响后世更深的是制度遗产——行省制与站赤驿站网络塑造了后世的行政区划与交通格局。至元三十一年（1294）世祖崩于大都，成宗继立，混一格局延续。对这位征服王朝皇帝，正统与汉地治理的评价历来撕裂，本页取中性叙述，其历史后效则无可争议。

bio_parts_en.value:
Kublai was the emperor who rewrote the Mongol khanate into a Chinese-style dynasty and completed the first grand unification since the fall of the Tang. This page takes 《元史·世祖本纪》 (juan 004–017) as its chronological backbone, with the conquest of the Song cross-checked against 《宋史·瀛国公纪》 and 《二王本纪》.

His opening act was a civil war over the khanship: in the first year of Zhongtong (1260) he took the throne as Great Khan at Kaiping and established the Zhongtong era, then immediately fought Ariq Böke for the succession and prevailed. Institutions for the Chinese territories advanced step by step thereafter: the era name changed in the first year of Zhiyuan (1264); in the eighth year of Zhiyuan (1271), taking the Yijing phrase "great is the qian origin," he proclaimed the dynastic name Great Yuan; and in the ninth year of Zhiyuan (1272) Zhongdu was renamed Dadu, fixing the political center in the land of Yan.

The destruction of the Song was the main thread of the middle of his reign: in the tenth year of Zhiyuan (1273) Xiangyang fell, opening the decisive gateway to the south; in the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan (1276) Bayan entered Lin'an, the Song court surrendered, and its remnants fled to the sea; and in the sixteenth year of Zhiyuan (1279) came the Battle of Yashan — the Song fell, and China was unified once more under the Yuan. Read against
, the page shows the long-range echo between two grand unifications; read against

, it shows the beginning and the end of the Zhao Song house.

His military reach also had its limits: in the eighteenth year of Zhiyuan (1281) he campaigned against Japan a second time, the eastern expedition fleet met a storm and was lost, and expansion suffered a check. What shaped later ages more deeply was the institutional legacy — the provincial (xingsheng) system and the zhanchi postal-relay network molded the administrative divisions and transport patterns of later dynasties. In the thirty-first year of Zhiyuan (1294) Shizu died at Dadu; Chengzong succeeded him, and the unified order continued. Assessments of this conquest-dynasty emperor — on legitimacy and on the governance of the Chinese territories — have long been sharply divided; this page adopts a neutral account, while his historical after-effects are beyond dispute.
